title: Intake-to-publication sprint checklist for new model additions
creator: Lina Chen
description: Sprint-level operational checklist to take a new model from intake through publication in the catalog, with coordinated benchmarks, docs, and comms. This ticket centralizes owner assignments, acceptance criteria, artifacts required for publishing, and a minimal-risk rollout plan for both Hosted API and Dedicated/Private customers. Goal: ship catalog entry + benchmark results + release notes + starter docs and announce with coordinated comms within the sprint window.
acceptance_criteria: Model entry created in catalog with metadata (architecture, intended uses, license, tags)
Benchmarks completed: latency p50/p95, throughput, quality evals on core prompt set; results uploaded to benchmark dashboard
Docs published: quickstart, API examples, migration notes (if applicable), limitations and safety guidance
Release notes drafted and reviewed by Eng/Design/Legal/Marketing and ready for publication
SDK examples and sample prompts added to examples repo and referenced in catalog entry
Support & CS playbook updated with common issues and recovery steps
Rollout checklist executed and smoke tests pass in hosted canary and staging dedicated pool
tasks: Intake review: confirm model artifact, license, and vetting checklist (owner: Lina)
Assign benchmark owner and test matrix (owner: Eng perf lead)
Create canonical prompt set for quality regression tests (owner: PM)
Run perf bench: cold start, KV-cache, batching scenarios; capture p50/p95 and cost per token (owner: Eng)
Design: produce catalog thumbnail, feature badge copy, and quick visual for docs (owner: Design)
Docs: write quickstart, API/SDK snippet, safety/limitations, and migration notes (owner: Docs)
Release notes: draft user-facing blurb + technical notes for API changelog (owner: PM)
Marketing: prepare announcement assets, one-pager, and blog draft (owner: Marketing)
Console: add dashboard panels for model metrics and link to alerting (owner: Observability)
Legal/Security: confirm license and privacy constraints; flag any data residency requirements (owner: Legal)
Support: update triage doc and Slack shortcuts; schedule 30-min handoff with CS (owner: Support)
Engineering: add integration tests and backward-compat checks; open release PR(s) (owner: Eng)
Release gating: run smoke tests in canary region, verify rollback path, sign-off (owner: PM/Eng)
Post-launch measurement: define KPIs and dashboard (usage, latency, error rate, cost per token) (owner: PM/Analytics)
updates: 2026-02-13: Intake paperwork completed; license is permissive MIT-style. Lina verified model checksum and uploaded artifacts to GCS.
2026-02-15: Benchmarks started. Initial latency p50 looks promising on rtx-A100 with quantized float16 profile. Eng set up batch size matrix.
2026-02-17: Design supplied three thumbnail options; PM selected option B for clarity in small UI contexts.
2026-02-18: Docs draft created at https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/PM-71288-docs-draft. Need a safety paragraph from Applied ML.
2026-02-19: Marketing prepared blog outline; proposed publish window 2026-03-10 to align with trade show. Waiting on final benchmark numbers.
2026-02-20: Smoke tests scheduled for 2026-02-25; Eng to create canary pool and tagging. Updated estimate to 5 story points.
rollout_steps: 1) Publish catalog draft behind feature flag (no public listing): notify internal beta list
2) Deploy model variant to staging and run smoke/perf/quality tests across regions
3) If smoke ok, enable canary for small percentage of traffic in hosted API; run 24-48h monitoring
4) Validate Dedicated/Private upgrade instructions and verify no API contract changes
5) Publish release notes and docs minutes before public catalog listing
6) Announce publicly via blog + social; coordinate marketing and partner comms
7) Monitor metrics for 72h and be ready to rollback or limit traffic to fallback model
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Benchmarks reveal high variance at long context lengths. Mitigation: document recommended max context and provide quantized variants; postpone public announcement until mitigations are in place.
Risk: License restrictions discovered late. Mitigation: Legal to approve or block; hold publish if license incompatible.
Risk: Safety/ hallucination failure modes on a known prompt family. Mitigation: add safety note, provide disallowed prompt examples, and mark model as beta in catalog.
Risk: Dedicated capacity requires specialized kernel that delays launch. Mitigation: ship hosted-only first with clear timeline for Dedicated support; notify customers.
Risk: SDK mismatch causes breaking sample code. Mitigation: pin SDK example versions and include migration snippet; coordinate SDK release with model publication.
